headline: Sworn in as President in Buffalo
summary: Arriving in Buffalo at 1:30 p.m. to find McKinley dead, Roosevelt takes the oath as the 26th President at 3:15 p.m. in Ansley Wilcox's library, the furniture still under summer dust covers. Judge John R. Hazel swears him in, wearing borrowed clothes that don't fit, with most of the Cabinet present. He asks Booker T. Washington to meet with him.

headline: First full day as President
summary: Roosevelt stays at the Wilcox house, attends a service for McKinley, and confers with Root, Knox, Odell and Littauer as McKinley lies in state at Buffalo City Hall. Edith brings the children home to Sagamore Hill, where a doctor finds a pebble in Quentin's sore ear; Archie has tonsillitis.

headline: Riding the funeral train to Washington
summary: Roosevelt travels to Washington aboard the train carrying McKinley's body, arriving at 8:30 p.m. Edith and Bamie follow on another train and stay at 1733 N Street, where Corinne and Douglas join them. Edith's diary says he looked grave and older.

headline: Crowds surge at the Capitol
summary: McKinley's body rests in the White House, where Grover Cleveland is among thousands of mourners. Roosevelt and Edith follow the hearse to the Capitol with Will Cowles; there the crowd bursts through barriers and police and soldiers force it back. That evening he holds a Cabinet meeting at 1733 N Street.

headline: Callers, a Taft profile and school worries
summary: Roosevelt sees Leonard Wood, Carroll D. Wright, Binger Hermann, Representatives Livingston and Dayton, and Senators Elkins and Scott. His article on Governor Taft runs in The Outlook. Edith writes that people are anxious about how the children will be schooled in Washington, and Roosevelt writes Gilder about a proposed biography.

headline: Settling into the White House
summary: Roosevelt begins work in the White House, signing papers all day on what would have been his father's birthday, which he takes as a good sign. His only dinner guests are his sisters, Bamie and Corinne, with their husbands.

tr_quotes.text: I have realized it as I signed various papers all day long, and I feel that it is a good omen.

headline: Moving into the White House
summary: Roosevelt formally settles in and receives Gage, Postmaster General Smith and Senators Penrose, Cockrell and Pritchard. Edith readies five family bedrooms and clears out decades of clutter; only Kermit and Ethel are there so far. He tells Lodge it would be worse to be morbid than to accept how he came to office.

headline: A ransom demand from Macedonia

headline: Keeping McKinley's promises
summary: On Corinne's 40th birthday, Roosevelt says he will honor McKinley's pledged appointments, tells Brooks Adams the U.S. must help balance European trade or risk war, and opposes a government-owned Pacific cable.

headline: Keeping McKinley's Cabinet
summary: Roosevelt keeps McKinley's entire Cabinet and meets Admiral Schley and Senators Proctor, Mitchell and Foraker. He writes Hay about an isthmian canal and tells Foraker he cannot campaign for him. Kermit and Archie start at Force public school, Ethel boards at the Cathedral School, and his article "With the Cougar Hounds" appears in Scribner's.
